name: Gullinbursti
body:
GULLINBURSTI
CR 11

An enormous boar with gleaming golden bristles, bright metallic tusks, and a radiant aura which shines like sunlight.

N Large magical beast (augmented construct)
Init +0; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent, true seeing; Perception +17

DEFENSE

AC 25, touch 9, flat-footed 25 (+16 natural, –1 size)
hp 149 (13d10+78)
Fort +14, Ref +10, Will +7; +2 vs. disease, mind–affecting effects, and poison
Defensive Abilities ferocity, DR 5/—; Immune blindness, dazzling effects, fatigue, exhaustion; SR 22

OFFENSE

Speed 100 ft.; air walk
Melee gore +22 (2d8+20)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks dazzling strike
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 12th; concentration +13)

Constant—air walk, daylight, true seeing

STATISTICS

Str 31, Dex 10, Con 23, Int 2, Wis 12, Cha 13
Base Atk +13; CMB +24 (+26 bull rush); CMD 34 (36 vs. bull rush, 38 vs. trip)
Feats Awesome Blow, Improved Bull Rush, Improved Vital Strike, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack, Vital Strike
Skills Perception +17
SQ living construct, powerful gore

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Dazzling Strike (Su)

When gullinbursti makes a gore attack, all sighted creatures within 15 feet must attempt a DC 22 Fortitude save. Those who fail are blinded for 2 rounds and dazzled for an additional 1d4 rounds; those who succeed are instead dazzled for 1d4 rounds. Creatures riding a gullinbursti, as well as those being drawn by one in a vehicle such as a chariot, are unaffected by this ability. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Living Construct (Ex)

The first gullinbursti were created beings, forged and then awakened with powerful magic. Gullinbursti gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against disease, mind-affecting effects, and poison. They are also immune to exhaustion and fatigue.

Powerful Gore (Ex)

Gullinbursti applies twice its Strength modifier to its gore damage.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold or temperate forests
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Gullinbursti are radiant, unearthly boars whose golden bristles shine with brilliant light. These creatures were forged and brought to life by the Dvergir, an ancient dwarven people renowned for their mastery of magical crafting. Gullinbursti are capable of natural reproduction but are exceptionally rare in the present age, in part due to a long gestation period which gives birth to only a single offspring.

Originally presented as a gift to a major deity, gullinburstis serve as tireless mounts and chariot beasts, able to race across land, sea, and sky with impossible speed. Their golden manes blaze like sunlight as they run, swifter than any horse and unhindered by darkness or terrain.

Gullinbursti means “golden-bristled”, reflecting its luminous metallic mane, but these creatures bear an alternate epithet Slíðrugtanni, meaning “dangerous tusk”, which speaks to their deadly natural weaponry and the fierce, untamed vitality that drives them.
